summary.intent: Conduct a security review of the feat/store-ipns-crypto-data-in-db branch, implement fixes for identified vulnerabilities, and get the PR merged with all CI checks passing.
summary.outcome: All HIGH/MEDIUM security findings were fixed (pubKey-to-ipnsName binding, web app base64 overflow, missing publicKey on publish, server-side validation, DTO MaxLength), CI was fixed by resolving ESM/CJS bundling conflicts for @cipherbox/crypto, all PR review comments were addressed, and the fixes were pushed to remote.

repo: The @cipherbox/crypto package is used by both NestJS (CJS consumer) and Vite/browser (ESM consumer), requiring a split tsup build config: CJS bundles all deps inline (noExternal: [/.*/]), ESM keeps deps external

IPNS names are cryptographically derived from Ed25519 public keys via deriveIpnsName() — a compromised server could substitute its own keypair and bypass signature verification without pubKey-to-ipnsName binding
The web app's ipns.service.ts was not sending publicKey on publish even though the API supported it, making server-side pubKey-to-ipnsName validation dead code for web-published records
The 'Verify API Spec' CI job was missing a build step for @cipherbox/crypto before running pnpm api:generate, causing it to fail on this branch
ipns.service.spec.ts used a dummy testIpnsName that didn't cryptographically match the test public key — the new server-side validation broke these tests

code.finding: pubKey-to-ipnsName binding check added here after signature verification — derives IPNS name from returned pubKey and compares to requested ipnsName
Spread operator on Uint8Array for base64 encoding causes call-stack overflow on large IPNS records — fixed with loop-based approach
Split into two defineConfig entries: CJS with noExternal bundling all deps (for Node/Jest), ESM with external deps (for Vite) — both DTS outputs needed
Test fixtures used fake IPNS name k51qzi5uqu5dg12345abcdef67890 — must derive real IPNS name from test public key using deriveIpnsName()
Verify API Spec job needs pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build before pnpm api:generate when crypto package has new dependencies

workflow: When bundling packages that need to work in both CJS (NestJS) and ESM (Vite) environments, split tsup configs are required — noExternal for CJS, external for ESM
Before pushing fixes that add new server-side validation, verify existing test fixtures are cryptographically consistent with the new validation logic
When adding a new workspace package dependency to an app, check if CI jobs that build that app have explicit build steps for the new dependency
Verify the API actually starts locally (not just compiles) before pushing — runtime ESM/CJS errors won't show up in tsc

friction: The noExternal: [/.*/] fix that solved the NestJS CJS problem immediately broke the Vite desktop build — required a second iteration with a split config
1Password SSH agent intermittently blocked git commit signing, requiring manual retry
CI was interrupted partway through, requiring the session to be resumed
Multiple CI iterations needed (3 pushes) to fully resolve the ESM/CJS bundling issue before the build was green
open_items: signatureVerified: false is returned when server omits signature fields but callers never enforce signatureVerified === true — the boolean is informational only (deferred by design decision)
Medium finding #5 (inconsistent key zeroization) was deferred as a convention issue rather than fixed

The @libp2p/* and @noble/* packages being bundled into @cipherbox/crypto's CJS output increases bundle size significantly (457KB) — may want to revisit if a proper CJS-compatible alternative becomes available
